transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you and what brings you here today?

I guess… it’s mostly something at work. When I see balloons at school, even from down the hallway, I kind of freeze. My chest gets tight right away, and it takes me a moment before I can think clearly about what I’m supposed to be doing.
Does this reaction happen only at work or school, or do you also feel this way when you see balloons in other places, like at home or in stores?
Mostly at school. That’s where I notice it right away—if I spot balloons, even down the hallway, I just… my chest tightens and I freeze for a second before I can think straight.
Do you ever feel this way when you see balloons at home, in stores, or in other places outside of school?

I haven’t really noticed it much outside of school. It’s more… when I’m at school and I spot balloons, even across the hallway, my chest gets tight and I sort of freeze for a moment before I can think.
Have you ever had this same reaction to balloons in places other than school, like at home, in stores, or at parties?
Not really… I mean, the thing I’m sure about is at school. If I see balloons there, even across the hallway, I tense up and my chest gets tight, and I kind of freeze for a moment.
When you’re not at school, like at home or walking through a store, do you ever notice the same reaction if you see balloons?
Not really that I’ve noticed. It’s mainly at school—if I see balloons, even from down the hall, I just kind of lock up for a second and my chest gets tight.
Have you ever reacted this way to balloons in any other setting outside of school that you haven’t mentioned yet, like at a friend's house or in a park?

I don’t think so. It’s really the school setting that I’m aware of… like the second I spot balloons there, even across the hallway, my chest tightens and I freeze for a moment before I can think straight.
Have you ever had any uncomfortable or fearful reactions to balloons in any other places besides school, even if it was just a little bit?
Not that I can really point to. It’s more… at school. When I spot balloons there, even down the hall, my chest tightens and I sort of freeze for a second before I can think clearly.
When you're not at school, such as at home, in a store, or at a party, do you ever feel anxious or react strongly to balloons in those places?
Not really… I don’t notice it much outside of school. It’s more that when I see balloons at school, even from across the hallway, I tense up—my chest gets tight and I kind of freeze for a moment.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain areas or situations at school to prevent seeing balloons?

Yeah… somewhat. Lately I’ve been asking my aides to take over birthday circles if there are balloons, or I’ll kind of move away from festival tables when they’re nearby. If I have to stay, I just keep my distance and try not to look at them.
